Tamales with Cheese and Peppers

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 8Prep 45 minCook 1 hour

Tamales with Cheese and Peppers are a beloved traditional dish served during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, celebrated on December 12th. These savory tamales combine the rich flavors of creamy cheese and mildly spicy peppers wrapped in masa dough, steamed to perfection, symbolizing community and faith during this important Mexican holiday.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 2 1/2 cups chicken broth (or vegetable broth)
  • 1 1/2 cups lard or vegetable shortening
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 2 cups queso fresco or mozzarella cheese, cut into small cubes
  • 4 roasted poblano peppers, peeled, seeded, and sliced
  • 30 dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Method

  1. Soak the dried corn husks in warm water for at least 30 minutes to soften them.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
  3. Add the lard or shortening to the masa mixture and beat with your hands or a mixer until the dough is light and fluffy.
  4. Gradually add the chicken broth while continuing to mix until the dough has a soft, spreadable consistency.
  5. Test the dough by dropping a small piece into cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If not, continue beating and adding a little more broth if needed.
  6. Drain the corn husks and pat dry. Spread about 2 tablespoons of masa dough evenly onto the smooth side of each husk, leaving a border at the edges.
  7. Place a few slices of roasted poblano pepper and a couple of cheese cubes in the center of the masa.
  8. Fold the sides of the husk inward to enclose the filling, then fold the bottom up and secure if needed.
  9. Arrange the tamales upright in a large steamer pot with water at the bottom, making sure the open ends face up.
  10. Cover the tamales with a damp cloth and steam over boiling water for about 60 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure water does not run dry.
  11. After cooking, let the tamales rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until charred for a smoky flavor.
  • If queso fresco is unavailable, mozzarella or Monterey Jack cheese are good substitutes.
  • Serve tamales with salsa verde or red salsa for added flavor.
